jobs.description:
About Minga

Minga means community. It’s the belief that we achieve more together than we ever could alone. At Minga, joining our team isn't just about a new role, it's about joining a collective that is deeply invested in your growth, your impact, and your connection to the people around you.

We’re building the Student Behavior Platform schools can’t live without, and we’re having fun doing it.

We are a tight-knit group of curious, low-ego humans who genuinely enjoy the "we" over the "me."

  • Supportive Growth: You aren’t on an island. You’ll have the autonomy to do your best work and a community that has your back every step of the way.
  • Shared Ownership:Whether at our Kelowna HQ or remote, you’re a vital part of a team that cares as much about the people as the product.
  • Real Impact: Everything we do supports the educators and students we serve, creating a ripple effect of connection in schools everywhere.

Ready to be part of the community?

Come help us make school life better for everyone. 💙

The Role

We’re not just hiring for a position, we’re adding a teammate

Reporting to the CRO the Director, Account Management owns Minga's post-sale commercial motion including retention, expansion, and customer health for the Account Management organization. The Director, Account Management will lead the x2 Managers, Account Management and are ultimately accountable for GRR, NRR, and the quality of every customer relationship in the book.

This is a leadership role that operates at two levels simultaneously: setting the strategic direction for how Minga retains and grows its customer base, and being close enough to the team to know when something needs to change before the data tells you. You are the bridge between the AM organization and the rest of the company, bringing the customer perspective to Product, partnering with Sales on the expansion motion, and reporting the commercial health of the book to the executive team.

What You’ll Do 🚀

Organizational Leadership

  • Lead and develop the x2 Managers, Account Management, setting the direction and performance standards for the function
  • Create a culture of ownership, proactivity, and commercial accountability across the Account Management team
  • As needed, support recruitment of talent into the management layer; build succession depth within the AM organization
  • Allocate resources across the AM team as the customer base and growth targets evolve

Revenue & Retention Strategy

  • Own the company's GRR and NRR targets; set the strategy for how the post-sale org delivers on them
  • Design and maintain the customer segmentation model — defining how accounts are tiered, resourced, and managed based on size, complexity, and strategic value
  • Build the early-warning and intervention system that catches churn risk before it becomes churn
  • Develop the upsell and expansion playbook in partnership with the Director of Sales — ensuring AM-identified opportunities convert through the AE motion

Customer Strategy & Advocacy

  • Lead the business review and QBR program; define the cadence and format by account tier
  • Own the advocacy and reference pipeline, building a network of champion districts that accelerate new sales
  • Represent the customer voice to the executive team and Product organization; translate retention patterns into actionable strategic input

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner with the Director of Sales on the AE ↔ AM expansion deal model. Clear lanes, clean collaboration, and no revenue left on the table
  • Work with Marketing and Customer Experience on customer marketing programs, case studies, and co-selling motions
  • Coordinate with the Implementation function to ensure AM handoffs from go-live are complete and actionable
  • Report AM team performance including GRR, NRR, health trends, churn analysis to the executive team on a regular cadence

What Success Looks Like 🎯

In the first 30 days:

  • Complete picture of the current AM book; health by tier, renewal pipeline, and team capacity
  • Relationships established with the Director of Sales, Director of Customer Experience, Product, and leadership team.
  • Assessment of the current touch model process and playbook, with a view on highest-impact improvements

In the first 90 days:

  • Updated customer segmentation model and resource allocation strategy for the AM team
  • GRR/NRR forecast presented to the executive team with confidence
  • Individual development plans in place for each AM in partnership with the Manager, Account Management

Ongoing:

  • Gross Revenue Retention (GRR)
  • Net Revenue Retention (NRR
  • Renewal rate
  • Healthy, growing advocate and reference pipeline
  • AM team retention - building an environment people want to stay and grow in

What We Require ✅

  • 5-8+ years in customer success or account management in B2B SaaS, with at least 3 years leading managers or senior leaders
  • Proven ownership of GRR and NRR at a company level, not just a team level
  • Experience building and scaling account management organizations in a named-book, renewal-focused model
  • Strategic thinker with the ability to design customer segmentation models, retention programs, and expansion motions
  • Strong cross-functional leadership - you've partnered effectively with Sales, Product, and Marketing to improve commercial outcomes
  • Excellent executive communication - you present performance data clearly and drive decisions at the leadership level
  • HubSpot or equivalent CRM and CS tooling experience
  • K-12 EdTech or education sector experience is a strong asset

Who You Are 🌟

  • A strategic owner - you see GRR and NRR as the outcomes of a system, and you build that system deliberately
  • A people developer - your managers are better leaders because of how you coach them
  • Commercially sharp and analytically driven, you make decisions based on data, not instinct alone
  • A connector - you hold the AE/AM expansion motion together and keep that seam clean and productive
  • A clear and confident communicator at the executive level, you don't just report results, you explain what's driving them and what you're doing about it
  • Mission-aligned - you believe that customer retention and customer success are the same thing, and that Minga's impact on schools depends on getting it right

Role Compensation 💰

OTE: $165,000-$205,000 + Equity

Compensation Philosophy & Transparency 💰

At Minga, we believe compensation should reflectimpact, fairness,and market alignment, supporting our mission to empower educators and students while building a high-performing, people-first culture. Our standard is to pay at or near the midpoint of the range unless there is a clear business rationale to vary. This approach allows for growth and provides room to learn and develop within the role. We also conduct annual compensation reviews in November, which take into account both market benchmarks and individual performance.

Check out our Benefits & Perk Page for a full review of the overall compensation package.

AI at Minga 🤖

At Minga, we believe AI should make your work faster, smarter, and less repetitive — not more complicated. AI is meant to augment how we work, not replace human thinking or judgment

  • Leverage AI, but stay you. We expect you to use the tools available to you, but remember that Minga is built on real people. Your resume and "Why Minga" answer will be read by a real life human, so give us a glimpse of the person behind the profile.
  • During your interview we value your unique voice over a perfect prompt. It's okay to not answer perfectly.

What You Can Expect From Us 💙

At Minga, you’re more than just an application, you’re a real person with a story we want to hear.

We believe in clear communication, mutual respect, and ensuring every candidate walks away feeling valued, whether we end up working together or not.

Ready to Apply? 👋

If this role feels like a fit or even a maybe,hit apply.

We’re genuinely excited to learn more about you. Let’s build something meaningful together.

Salary: $165,000 to $205,000 OTE + Equity

jobs.excerpt: DataKind is looking for a Full Stack Software Engineer!
jobs.description:
DataKind is looking for a Full Stack Software Engineer!

DataKind is looking for a values-driven, product-focused full stack software engineer who is ready to make a major impact on student graduation rates by building the web application and API layer that powers our education data platform. If you're someone who moves fluidly between frontend and backend, cares about the craft of a well-built data product, and are committed to advancing equity through data, we want to bring you on board!

Location

This is a remote position that can be based anywhere in the U.S. and requires the majority of working hours each day to fall between 8am and 6pm Eastern Standard Time.

Salary Range

The salary range is $85,000 - 90,000 annually.

Actual salary within these ranges will be based on the candidate's experience and internal salary equity scan of active employee(s) with similar role and experience.

About the Opportunity

DataKind is seeking a Full Stack Software Engineer to build and evolve the UI and API layer of our education data platform. This role owns the software that turns complex educational data into something usable, insightful, and reliable for the institutions we serve. You'll spend most of your time in the web application and API, with regular contributions to the data engineering and infrastructure work that supports it.

Reporting to the VP of Technology, you'll work closely with Data Engineering, Data Science, Product, and Customer Success to ship features that directly affect student outcomes. You'll be a contributing senior technical voice on the team, someone who can take ambiguous product requirements and turn them into shipped, well-architected software.

What You'll Do

Product Engineering (60%)

  • Design, build, and maintain web application front end and the APIs that power it.
  • Translate product and user requirements, often shaped by direct partner feedback, into clean, maintainable, well-tested code.
  • Own features end to end: from technical design through implementation, testing, and deployment.
  • Collaborate with Product and Customer Success to understand how institutional users actually work with our education data platform and use that to inform technical decisions.
  • Contribute to frontend architecture, component design, and API design standards across the team.

Data Engineering and Infrastructure (25%)

  • Contribute to data pipeline and integration work that feeds the education data platform, in partnership with the Data Engineering team.
  • Support infrastructure decisions related to application performance, scalability, and reliability.
  • Help ensure data flowing into the application layer is validated, well-structured, and secure, including implementation of authentication/authorization (e.g., SSO, OAuth, role-based access control) appropriate for handling sensitive student data.

Collaborate and contribute across DataKind (15%)

  • Partner with Data Engineering and Data Science to operationalize models and analytics into production-ready product features.
  • Align your work with DataKind’s engineering standards, conduct timely code reviews for your peers, and consistently contribute quality technical documentation.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement and maintenance of internal tooling, engineering process documentation, and workflow automation.

Qualifications

Required

  • Deep alignment with DataKind's mission and values, and demonstrated commitment to educational equity and data-driven social impact
  • 3-5 years of professional full stack software engineering experience, including meaningful ownership of both frontend and backend systems.
  • Advanced proficiency in a modern JavaScript/TypeScript framework (e.g., React) and backend API development.
  • Working proficiency in GCP, Python and SQL to support infrastructure and data engineering pipelines.
  • Experience designing and building RESTful or GraphQL APIs.
  • Experience writing automated tests (unit, integration, and/or end-to-end) and working in a codebase with CI-enforced test coverage.
  • Solid understanding of data modeling and how application design intersects with data pipelines.
  • Proven ability to collaborate across engineering, data science, and product functions.
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred

  • Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related technical field.
  • Experience with PHP, Laravel, OpenAI API, and Anthropic API.
  • Experience with Git-based collaborative workflows (e.g., pull requests, code reviews) and CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitHub Actions).
  • Experience building or integrating AI-powered features into a product (e.g., LLM integration, recommendation systems, applied ML).
  • Experience implementing authentication and authorization patterns (e.g., SSO, OAuth, role-based access control) in a production web application.
  • Experience building dashboards or data visualization tools for varied end users.
  • Familiarity with education data systems (e.g., SIS, LMS, or student outcome data).
  • Experience building systems that comply with SOC2 and/or FERPA.
  • Familiarity with civic tech, social impact, or nonprofit data ecosystems.

About DataKind

At DataKind, we believe in the transformative power of data science and AI to create a more promising future. Since our founding in 2012, we've been at the forefront of designing scalable, data-driven tools that address some of the world's toughest challenges—ranging from frontline health, humanitarian action, climate and environment, economic opportunity, education, and more. As both a product innovator and a movement catalyst, we set new standards in the social sector, empowering organizations to harness the full potential of data science and AI while putting communities first.

Why Work with DataKind

At DataKind, we believe that people are the most important asset to delivering on our mission. As a people-first remote organization, we offer the following for all our employees:

  • Flexibility and time off. Enjoy genuine flexibility that goes beyond adjustable hours. We build in shared time off, organization-wide recharge days, bi-weekly meeting-free days, and flexible PTO (with a minimum of 20 vacation days encouraged annually).
  • Comprehensive Wellness Support. We care for your total wellbeing with 100% employer-paid medical, vision, and dental benefits for employees (72% for dependents), a wellness reimbursement program for the activities and purchases that matter to you, and 12 weeks paid parental leave when you need it most.
  • A Culture of Growth. Every team member receives professional development funding each year, alongside mentorship and advancement opportunities. We invest in your future with a 401(k) plan with 5% employer matching.
  • Meaningful Connection. Despite being distributed across time zones, we value being able to come together in person for conferences, strategic planning, and at our annual staff retreat.
  • Living our Values. DataKind is committed to a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment in our day-to-day work and via special initiatives driven by our DEI Steering Committee.

DataKind is an Equal Opportunity Employer

DataKind is an equal opportunity employer and strongly encourages candidates from underrepresented groups in tech to apply. DataKind does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, disability, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected category.

Applicants must have a U.S.-based permanent address and currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis indefinitely without employer visa sponsorship.

Senior Manager - Security Engineering

Department: Ferguson, Information Security

Reports To: Director, Information Security

The Senior Manager, Security Engineering provides vision, leadership, and operational accountability for Ferguson’s enterprise security engineering capabilities. This role leads the teams and services responsible for identifying, reducing, and reporting technology risk across applications, infrastructure, cloud platforms, endpoints, identity-integrated services, email, edge protections, and emerging AI-enabled attack surfaces. The leader is accountable for ensuring Ferguson has the people, processes, tooling, and partnerships required to continuously assess risk, harden technology baselines, validate defenses, support secure delivery, and drive remediation in partnership with Technology, Security, business, and third-party participants. This position requires deep technical judgment, collaborative leadership, and operational rigor. It also requires the ability to translate complex security risks into actionable priorities. These priorities help Ferguson complete its business plans securely.

Location: This role is approved to be either Remote within the United States or Hybrid for associates in Newport News, VA, in accordance with company policy.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Leadership and Strategy (40%)

  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Security Engineering team through recruiting, hiring, coaching, mentorship, performance management, and career development.
  • Define and maintain the operating model, service ownership, roadmap, and measurable objectives related to Security Engineering capabilities across vulnerability management, DevSecOps, penetration testing, edge security, email security, endpoint security, cloud and configuration posture, and related engineering services.
  • Represent Security Engineering performance, risks, resource needs, and strategic opportunities with Information Security leadership and multi-functional Technology leadership forums.
  • Partner with Security Architecture, Security Operations, GRC, Identity, Infrastructure, Application Development, Cloud, and business technology teams to align engineering priorities to enterprise risk reduction and business enablement.
  • Continuously assess team skills, capacity, vendor support, and tooling maturity against current and emerging threats, including AI-enabled attack techniques and post-quantum readiness considerations.
  • Drive a culture of secure-by-default engineering, shared accountability, transparency, and practical risk-based decision making across Ferguson technology teams.
  • Establish clear metrics, performance indicators, reporting routines, and executive-ready narratives that communicate risk posture, control effectiveness, remediation progress, service value, and investment needs.

Security Engineering Management (60%)

  • Own and mature Security Engineering service areas including vulnerability management, DevSecOps, penetration testing and adversarial validation, edge security, email security, endpoint detection and response, cloud security posture, configuration risk, application security testing, and security tooling integrations.
  • Lead Ferguson’s risk-based vulnerability management capability, ensuring asset visibility, authenticated scanning, application and infrastructure assessment, risk contextualization, remediation tracking, exception management, and leadership reporting are operating effectively.
  • Advance secure software delivery by integrating security testing and guidance into development workflows, including static analysis, software composition analysis, container security, secrets protection, code signing, secure repository practices, and developer-facing remediation support.
  • Run penetration testing, AI-enabled security testing, purple team support, and continuous adversarial validation activities for critical applications, APIs, external assets, cloud services, identity entry points, and business-critical technology platforms.
  • Ensure public-facing applications and digital channels are protected through effective use of edge security capabilities, including WAF, bot management, CDN security, origin protection, API protections, and secure traffic patterns.
  • Provide engineering ownership and oversight for email and endpoint security capabilities, including migration planning, policy tuning, telemetry quality, detection support, deployment health, and operational readiness.
  • Drive enterprise configuration and posture management across cloud, infrastructure, endpoints, applications, and identity-adjacent services to identify deviations from hardened baselines and support timely remediation.
  • Partner with Identity, PAM, SSO, certificate, and non-human identity teams where security engineering capabilities depend on identity controls, privileged access, machine identity, key management, or cryptographic services.
  • Support pivotal initiatives such as AI resilience, post-quantum readiness, enterprise cryptographic visibility, secrets removal, cloud posture modernization, and security tooling rationalization.
  • Ensure Security Engineering platforms and service offerings are reliable, monitored, documented, supportable, and aligned with published policies, standards, organizational change expectations, and regulatory or audit obligations.
  • Establish and maintain runbooks, customer concern paths, operational handoffs, service ownership documentation, vendor engagement models, and cross-training practices to prevent coverage gaps.
  • Prioritize engineering work based on business risk, exploitability, asset criticality, exposure, compliance requirements, operational impact, and available remediation capacity.
  • Partner with Technology teams to close visibility and deployment gaps in required security tooling so Ferguson can assess and protect operational assets consistently.
  • Contribute technical requirements to security technology selection, proof-of-value efforts, vendor evaluations, architecture reviews, and implementation planning.
  • Actively monitor new and emerging technologies, threats, attack patterns, regulatory expectations, and industry practices to assess their applicability to Ferguson’s security engineering program.
  • Perform other duties or functions as requested by management.
  • Drive and report on Service restoration activities as required.
  • Support enterprise business and sales objectives through the effective and efficient performance of job responsibilities

Qualifications and Requirements:

  • Experience leading information security engineering, application security, vulnerability management, cloud security, endpoint security, or related technical security teams is required.
  • Experience managing full-time associates, contractors, vendors, and multi-functional delivery partners is required.
  • Experience building or operating risk-based vulnerability management, application security testing, DevSecOps, penetration testing, security tooling, or cloud posture management programs is strongly preferred.
  • Experience partnering with infrastructure, application development, cloud, identity, security operations, GRC, and business technology teams to reduce enterprise technology risk is strongly preferred.

  • Solid understanding of modern security tooling such as vulnerability scanners, risk reporting platforms, SAST, SCA, container security, WAF, bot management, EDR, CSPM, SIEM integrations, secrets management, certificate management, and identity-related security platforms.
  • Ability to lead multi-functional remediation efforts where ownership, technical complexity, business impact, and risk acceptance decisions must be coordinated across teams.
  • Knowledge of security frameworks, standards, and practices such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001/27002, OWASP, MITRE ATT&CK, CIS Benchmarks, secure SDLC, and IT service management.

jobs.description:
TeamViewer provides a leading Digital Workplace platform that connects people with technology—enabling, improving and automating digital processes to make work work better. Our software solutions harness the power of AI and shape the future of digitalization.

We believe that our diverse teams and strong company culture are key to the success of our products and technologies, that hundreds of millions of users around the world and around 645,000 customers across all industries rely on. With more than 1,900 employees worldwide, we celebrate the unique perspectives and talents that each individual brings to the table and foster a dynamic work environment where new ideas thrive. Are you ready to join our team and make an impact?

You'll own a book of roughly 100 existing Enterprise customers across the Northeast — about $4M in ARR — and you'll be measured on what you do with it: how fast customers reach real adoption, how cleanly they renew, and how much you grow them.

This is a high-velocity motion. You're not nursing a handful of accounts through year-long cycles; you're keeping a wide book moving — spotting the renewal that needs attention three quarters early, the team that's underusing what they bought, the adjacent use case nobody's asked about yet. Breadth is the job. The best people in this seat are organized, proactive, and relentless about working the whole book rather than the five accounts that shout loudest.

You're measured against three things, the same three every Enterprise AM is measured against:

  • Time to value — getting customers to meaningful adoption and depth of use inside what they already own. You drive this; you don't wait for it.

  • Secure renewal — retention, multi-year capture, and forecast accuracy across your book.

  • Upsell and cross-sell — expansion within your existing customers: more users, adjacent products, new use cases inside the relationships you already hold.

When an expansion grows large enough that running it well would pull you off the other 99 accounts, you partner with an Account Executive who runs that single cycle while you keep the rest of the book healthy. You source it, set it up, hand it off cleanly, and step back in as the relationship owner when it closes. Knowing when to pass and passing well is part of doing this job at a high level — it's how you protect the book, not a limit on what you close.

What good looks like in year one:

  • You know your book cold — which accounts are healthy, which are quietly at risk, and where the next expansion is hiding — without being asked.

  • Renewals are forecast accurately and captured early, not scrambled in the final 30 days.

  • You're generating expansion across the book consistently, not leaning on whichever pillar is easiest.

  • Your customers describe you as the steady, proactive presence who made the product work for them — not the person who showed up at renewal.

What you bring:

  • 2–4 years in Account Management, Customer Success, or a comparable customer-facing commercial role, ideally in B2B SaaS.

  • A track record of carrying retention and expansion targets, not just managing relationships.

  • The discipline to run a wide book — prioritizing across many accounts, not going deep on a few.

  • Clear, direct communication with customers and internal partners, especially at the handoff between teams.

  • Comfort with CRM hygiene and accurate forecasting as a core habit, not an afterthought.

  • Experience selling or supporting IT, security, or remote-connectivity software.

  • A history of partnering with AEs or sales counterparts on larger deals.

  • Multi-year and multi-product expansion experience.

  • Required Travel: Up to 40% domestic

What we offer:

  • Work location is Remote, USA.

  • Flexible PTO and paid holidays

  • 401(k) with employer matching

  • Comprehensive Health insurance package including 100% employer-paid medical coverage

  • Quarterly teambuilding events, leadership luncheons, and companywide “All Hands” meetings

  • Open door policy and business casual dress code

  • We celebrate diversity as one of our core values. Join c-a-r-e and lead change initiatives together with us!

Join Us! Let’s build the future of Delta Commercial together.

At Delta Commercial, we are building more than just products - we are designing solutions that transform spaces into commercial plumbing segments such as healthcare, education, public facilities, and office buildings. This is your opportunity to grow your career with an industry leader in design, innovation, and quality, while making a meaningful impact across the U.S. commercial landscape.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Business Development Manager (BDM), Heavy Commercial, is responsible for executing business growth plans for Delta Commercial. This individual is a key point of contact for manufacturing agency partners and is integral to building specification presence in their respective markets. The BDM will have strong relationships with commercial and institutional specifiers, mechanical contractors, architects, designers, facilities managers, and other stakeholders, positioning Delta Commercial as a top choice of these professionals.

At The Obama Foundation, our mission is to inspire, empower, and connect people to change their world. We seek to build an active democratic culture where people are equipped and motivated to make change in the communities where they live, work, and play. Right here on the South Side of Chicago, we’re building a home for this vision, a global center for change with a range of opportunities - coordinated programming, community outreach events, educational moments, and more - that invite visitors from down the block or across the globe to turn hope into action.

Achieving our ambitious goals starts with an exceptional team built on our Hope to Action Values - Courage, Empathy, Integrity, Accountability, Community, Inclusivity, Pragmatism, Resilience, Imagination, and Hope. A Framework that anyone, anywhere, can use to build trust, activate participation, and expand opportunity in their community.

Purpose of the Role

The Deputy Director for Global Programs, US Lead reports to the Director, Leaders Program and plays an integral role in leading the design and implementation of the Leaders USA program in service of the Obama Foundation’s mission to inspire, empower, and connect the next generation of leaders.

Core Job Responsibilities

  • Program Management: Design, implement, and manage Leaders USA programming, both virtual and in-person. Collaborate with Global Programs and Strategic Learning team members to refine a shared values-driven leadership development curriculum that incorporates equity in the design process and is customized for regional audiences and contexts. Align program content and design elements across all Obama Leaders programs, sharing best practices and resources. Provide rationale for appropriate regional differentiations.

  • Participant Selection: Implement the application and selection process for the Leaders USA program. Lead the review and selection of an inclusive, diverse, highly skilled cohort of emerging leaders. Refine the process after each application cycle.

  • Global Programs Collaboration: Work closely with the Impact and Insights Team to facilitate design, monitoring, evaluation, and learning activities to evaluate program impact. Actively bring ideas for operational improvements and provide feedback to the Program Operations team. Serve as an active member of the Managers sub-team, working collaboratively across program verticals to learn from each other and identify operational efficiencies.

  • Cross-Team Collaboration: Actively seek early input from and partnership with Foundation departments. Contribute to communications materials for donors, the board, the general public, and other stakeholders. Support Development through programming opportunities and conversations with donors and prospects. Work with Finance, Legal, Procurement, and other infrastructure teams early and often on operational changes and/or challenges in a spirit of partnership.

  • External Partnerships: Build and maintain partnerships with a broad set of organizations, institutions, and individuals, both inside and outside of the region, to build networks that support the execution of shared strategies and programming. Serve as regional representative and internal liaison regarding issues and relationships across the United States and territories.

  • Vendor Management: Research and identify program speakers, facilitators, consultants, and other partners (with an emphasis on thought leaders from the region). Facilitate the timely and successful completion of delegated activities and deliverables by vendors. Ensure that contracts are accurate and adhere to the guidelines and requirements established by Legal, Procurement, and other relevant departments.

  • Alumni Engagement: Contribute to the design and implementation of the alumni engagement strategy in collaboration with the Global Programs Network team. Support the integration of program alumni into related activities. Assist with alumni relationship management efforts and programming. When possible, support and plan cross-cohort alumni programming for issue-based and/or geographic cohorts.

  • People Management: Manage the workflow, deliverables, and performance of two Associates. Partner with them in setting and achieving high-impact individual and team-wide goals. Coach reports on project management and support them in increasing the quality, difficulty, and pace of their work. Develop their ability to tackle increasingly challenging opportunities independently.

  • Finance: Create and manage a detailed sub-team budget. Serve as a fiscally responsible steward of Foundation resources. Look for opportunities to reduce costs while maintaining program quality.

Key Deliverables / Outcomes

  • Deliver values-based leadership programming for multiple perspectives across the country, through collaborative curriculum design and best-practice alignment.

  • Directly manage and coach staff to achieve high-impact performance goals while increasing their independent project management capabilities.

  • Manage an inclusive and iterative selection process to recruit a diverse cohort of 50 emerging leaders for the USA program.

  • Analyze and strengthen program impact and drive operational improvements through cross-functional collaboration within global leadership teams.

  • Establish strategic collaborations with the Obama Presidential Center to integrate campus assets into Leaders USA virtual, hybrid, and in-person programming.

  • Execute cross-functional partnerships and produce high-quality communication materials to support organizational alignment, donor development, and operational efficiency.

  • Develop a robust network of regional and global institutional partners to facilitate shared strategies and enhance the Foundation's representation across the USA.

  • Successfully manage vendor relationships and contracts to ensure the timely delivery of specialized program content and adherence to organizational compliance standards.

  • Manage the sub-team budget to optimize resources and reduce costs while maintaining program quality.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience in facilitation and curriculum development, including designing engaging virtual and in person learning experiences, delivering training sessions to diverse audiences with a particular focus on participants with a wide breadth of viewpoints from across the USA, and evaluating program effectiveness to drive continuous improvement.

  • 4-6 years experience leading or supporting social impact or leadership programs, particularly with members in and across the USA.

  • Demonstrated experience developing content for stakeholder engagement and leading high-level virtual and in-person programming in collaboration with multiple partners.

  • Strong verbal and written skills, including the ability to foster trusting relationships with program participants of all backgrounds.

  • Detail-oriented process-thinker with skills in project management, budget, contract, and relationship management linked to a growing and global network.

The salary range for this role is between $110,000-$118,000.

This is a remote position with preference for candidates located in Chicago. Candidates in other locations are encouraged to apply.

This is a full-time, benefits-eligible position. Please note that employment in this role is contingent upon continued grant funding and is subject to annual budget reviews.

jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Hanwha Renewables, headquartered in Irvine, California, a member of Hanwha Group, a FORTUNE Global 500 firm that is among the eight largest business enterprises in South Korea. Hanwha Renewables designs, builds and manages renewable energy solutions. The company brings a decade of global leadership in renewable energy to North America, combining best-of-world technology, processes, and partnerships to deliver utility-grade energy solutions customized for local energy markets. Hanwha Renewables offers the full spectrum of energy solutions – from power plant development, design, construction, operations, and maintenance. With proven capabilities across the renewable energy value chain, Hanwha Renewables minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Power Marketing Analyst will support the analysis of power market trends, risk assessment, regulatory developments, and other insights that inform the company's power marketing and origination strategy for its solar and energy storage project development portfolio. The role supports the sourcing and execution of offtake opportunities for utility-scale solar, energy storage, and hybrid projects, and helps the Origination & Power Marketing team build strategic partnerships with utilities and other load-serving entities (LSEs) around Power Purchase and Energy Storage Tolling agreements, and alternative revenue structures such as Development Asset Transfers and Build-Transfer Agreements. The ideal candidate brings commercial and regulatory experience in utility-scale solar and energy storage, along with a strong understanding of market dynamics and shifting trends in energy procurement among major offtakers.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Power Marketing and Origination, this role is responsible for data analysis, market research, and coordination with cross-functional teams to help prepare proposals and optimize origination strategies. Over time, the Analyst will develop experience across:

  • The development cycle of new utility-scale solar and energy storage projects
  • New market strategy for greenfield campaigns
  • Future procurement trends of major LSEs, including through Integrated Resource Plans (IRPs)
  • Evolving contracting mechanisms in the solar and storage space
  • Targeted M&A activity

Strong analytical skills, developing market knowledge, and the ability to communicate findings clearly are essential for success in this role. This position is expected to travel up to 10% of the time.

The employee may be required to perform other job-related duties as requested by management. All duties will be assigned in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support execution of client engagement and power marketing strategies across the U.S.
  • Maintain business-tracking systems, including CRM platforms, RFP trackers, and related tools.
  • Prepare or support preparation of presentations for executive and customer briefings.
  • Monitor, track, and summarize load-serving entities' integrated resource and procurement plans.
  • Monitor and help evaluate opportunities across U.S. markets — such as RFPs for potential renewable and energy storage projects — and document and track them for future reference.
  • Coordinate proposal preparation in response to RFPs and bilateral opportunities by identifying, collecting, and organizing required information from subject matter experts across the organization.
  • Monitor public information on executed power purchase, tolling, build-transfer, and related agreements, and document relevant details in shared drive folders and trackers.
  • Monitor RTO and other market working groups for rule changes related to transmission rights, deliverability, and energy markets.
  • Monitor trade associations for relevant regulatory and market developments and share information across the team and organization as appropriate.
  • Assist in modeling and evaluating the impact of market design and topological changes — such as new generation, new storage, and transmission buildouts — on procurement opportunities and future energy prices.
  • Support forecasting of nodal/zonal and OTC energy prices for RTO and bilateral markets across long-term time horizons using fundamental and third-party models and services.
  • Participate as appropriate in standing and ad hoc internal and external meetings.
  • Communicate clearly and succinctly with audiences of different backgrounds during meetings and presentations.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in business, engineering, sustainability, finance, or a related field.
  • Minimum 1–3 years of relevant work experience in the electric utility industry's regulatory or commercial sector.
  • Familiarity with CRM applications and industry platforms such as F1, Procore, LevelTen, Aurora, NPM, or similar tools is a plus.
  • Coursework in at least one of the following areas: power system analysis, power system economics, power system operations and planning, optimization, data analysis, or object-oriented programming. If no relevant coursework, relevant work experience is also considered.
  • Working knowledge of organized and bilateral electricity markets across the U.S.; familiarity with at least one ISO/RTO market is preferred.

COMPENSATION: $90,000 - $105,000 salary

jobs.excerpt: About OpenSesameOpenSesame is transforming workforce development with an AI-powered marketplace of skill-building courses and learning pathways.
jobs.description:
About OpenSesame

OpenSesame is transforming workforce development with an AI-powered marketplace of skill-building courses and learning pathways. We help organizations build skills and stay compliant through a high-quality content catalog, seamless LMS/LXP integrations, and advanced capabilities like skills-based curation and multilingual content creation. More than 2,000 companies, including 150+ of the Global 2000, rely on OpenSesame to develop the world's most productive and admired workforces.
Learn more:

About the Revenue Operations Team

The OpenSesame Revenue Operations team is the operational backbone and growth catalyst of the company, enabling our Go-To-Market teams to sell, serve, and scale with clarity and confidence. We design the systems, processes, and insights that turn strategy into execution and ensure revenue flows efficiently from first conversation to renewal.

We partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Partners, Finance, and Legal to remove friction, enforce smart governance, and create a consistent, high-quality customer experience. Our work blends data, process, technology, and judgment to help the business move faster, without cutting corners.

What makes our Revenue Operations team unique:

  • We embrace automation and AI to reduce manual work, surface insights faster, and scale best practices.
  • We invest deeply in operational excellence and continuous improvement, balancing speed with discipline.
  • We are systems thinkers and problem solvers, motivated by making complex processes simpler and more scalable.
  • We measure success by business outcomes: deal velocity, forecast accuracy, won revenue and customer experience.
  • We operate with an owner’s mindset, taking accountability for results, not just activity.
  • We do the right thing, even when it requires tough conversations or slowing down a deal to protect the business.
  • We communicate with clarity and credibility, serving as trusted advisors to GTM teams and leadership.
  • We believe the best results come from tight collaboration and shared learning, supporting one another through peer problem-solving, documentation, and knowledge-sharing so the entire organization gets better together.

About the Sales Operations Manager, Direct Sales role:

The Sales Operations Manager, Direct Sales is the operational partner responsible for helping the AE organization generate revenue with greater clarity, discipline, speed, and predictability.

This is a manager-level individual contributor role with no direct reports. The role partners closely with Sales leadership, Revenue Operations, Enablement, Finance, Business Systems, SDR, and Marketing to improve how the Direct Sales motion runs from lead and opportunity management through Closed Won.

This is not a reporting-only role or a tactical support desk. The right person will diagnose what is slowing sellers down, pressure-test pipeline and forecast assumptions, identify where process or data is breaking down, and lead operational changes that improve sales execution.

Success in this role means Sales leaders trust the forecast, managers have clear operating views, sellers understand what good looks like, and the business can see where the pipeline is healthy, where risk exists, and where to focus next.

Performance Objectives

Establish Clarity and Trust (First 30 Days)

  • Build a deep understanding of the Direct Sales motion, including lead flow, opportunity management, pipeline creation, forecast cadence, sales stages, handoffs, and performance drivers.
  • Establish strong relationships with Sales leadership, frontline managers, SDR Ops, Enablement, Finance, Marketing, Business Systems, and Analytics.
  • Audit lead and opportunity management processes to identify gaps in adoption, stage integrity, forecast visibility, seller efficiency, and manager accountability.
  • Assess pipeline health, CRM hygiene, forecast accuracy, close-date discipline, territory design, quota coverage, and seller tool adoption.
  • Identify the highest-impact opportunities to reduce seller friction through process simplification, automation, AI-enabled workflows, or better reporting.
  • Deliver a current-state assessment with prioritized recommendations, including quick wins and longer-term improvements.

Build Operational Rigor (60 Days)

  • Refine lead and opportunity workflows to improve pipeline quality, accountability, and forecast reliability.
  • Implement pipeline hygiene standards, including stage criteria, aging thresholds, next-step expectations, close-date discipline, and forecast category guidance.
  • Establish a consistent pipeline inspection and forecasting cadence with Sales leadership and frontline managers.
  • Build manager-owned operating rhythms so Sales Ops enables accountability without becoming the long-term owner of seller follow-up.
  • Deliver actionable insights on funnel conversion, sales velocity, win rates, stage progression, deal quality, and rep/segment performance.
  • Scope automation or AI-enabled opportunities that reduce manual work, improve data quality, or surface risk faster.
  • Partner with Business Systems and Enablement to support CRM/workflow improvements, rollout readiness, seller communication, and adoption.

Scale Predictability and Impact (90+ Days)

  • Own ongoing pipeline health, stage integrity, forecast inspection, and adoption standards across the Direct Sales motion.
  • Improve forecast confidence by identifying risk early and surfacing root causes tied to process, coverage, deal quality, seller behavior, or market dynamics.
  • Establish durable reporting and inspection views for sellers, managers, Sales leadership, Finance, and RevOps.
  • Assess territory, quota, capacity, and account coverage models; provide recommendations aligned to growth plans.
  • Surface repeatable insights on ICP fit, account prioritization, deal quality, source performance, and conversion drivers.
  • Build feedback loops with Marketing, SDR Ops, Partners, Product, Enablement, and CS based on field data and funnel performance.
  • Drive measurable improvements in tool adoption, seller efficiency, sales cycle visibility, pipeline quality, and forecast accuracy.
  • Be viewed by Sales leadership as a trusted operating partner who brings clarity, urgency, and practical solutions.

Ongoing Responsibilities

Pipeline, Forecasting & Deal Inspection

  • Own pipeline health, stage integrity, and inspection frameworks across the Direct Sales motion.
  • Lead or support weekly forecasting cadence with Sales leadership and frontline managers.
  • Pressure-test forecast assumptions using stage progression, deal aging, close-date movement, next steps, source quality, ICP fit, and historical conversion.
  • Identify forecast risk early and surface root causes tied to process, coverage, deal quality, seller behavior, or market dynamics.

Sales Process, Tool Adoption & Change Management

  • Diagnose seller friction across CRM workflows, sales tools, lead/opportunity processes, and handoffs.
  • Build scalable processes that improve seller productivity without creating unnecessary administrative burden.
  • Drive adoption of core sales tools and processes through stakeholder alignment, enablement, manager reinforcement, and adoption tracking.
  • Partner with Enablement to create clear, practical training and reinforcement materials.

Automation, AI & Seller Efficiency

  • Identify opportunities to use automation and AI-enabled workflows to reduce manual work, improve data quality, and surface insights faster.
  • Partner with Business Systems, Analytics, and Enablement to scope, test, and roll out workflows that improve seller and manager productivity.
  • Explore use cases such as CRM update support, call/note summarization, pipeline risk detection, qualification validation, account prioritization, manager inspection summaries, executive forecast summaries, and seller prep automation.
  • Measure whether automation and AI-enabled workflows improve adoption, efficiency, pipeline quality, forecast confidence, or sales cycle performance.

Territory, Quota, Capacity & Account Strategy

  • Design, maintain, and recommend improvements to territory and account assignment models.
  • Partner with Sales leadership, Finance, Analytics, and SDR Ops on quota modeling, capacity planning, and coverage analysis.
  • Evaluate account potential, whitespace, greenspace, ICP fit, historical performance, pipeline coverage, rep capacity, and segment dynamics.
  • Support quarterly and annual planning through scenario modeling and data-backed recommendations.

Performance & Funnel Analytics

  • Analyze sales cycle, conversion rates, win rates, velocity, source performance, and deal quality by segment, source, territory, and rep cohort.
  • Diagnose performance gaps rooted in process, ICP fit, coverage, source quality, handoff quality, or deal execution patterns.
  • Translate complex data into clear recommendations for Sales leadership and cross-functional partners.
  • Build executive-ready narratives that explain what happened, why it happened, what is at risk, and what action should be taken.

Business Systems Partnership

  • Serve as the business owner for Direct Sales process requirements while partnering with Business Systems on technical configuration and implementation.
  • Translate field needs into clear business requirements.
  • Support UAT, rollout readiness, seller communication, and post-launch adoption tracking.
  • Ensure systems changes are practical, scalable, and aligned to how sellers and managers actually work.

You might notice we don’t have the typical list of requirements and buzzwords here. That’s intentional.

We’re looking for proven examples from your career that show you can do this job — that you’ve built systems, driven alignment, and created impact at scale. When you look back a year from now, you’ll know you’ve made OpenSesame better, faster, and stronger because of your leadership.

Although it should go without saying (but it doesn’t), OpenSesame is an equal opportunity employer and we strive to create a welcoming, inclusive environment that celebrates diversity.

We use AI. For real. Every team at OpenSesame works with AI tools daily, not as a buzzword, but as practice. You'll build fluency that most companies are still talking about adopting, with hands-on training and clear guardrails to experiment responsibly. AI amplifies your creativity and judgment. It doesn't replace them. The skills you build here travel with you.

Location: This position can be based anywhere in the US. We operate as a remote-first company, and invest in mandatory all-company meetings several times a year in addition to required team travel as necessary.

Performance Driven: We're looking for self-starters with a track record of delivering excellent results, but we're highly selective about who we hire. We don't focus on typical job requirements, instead, we're interested in specific examples from your past experiences. All positions can be based anywhere in the US, and require up to 15 days of travel per year, with senior management and leadership teams requiring up to 35 days.

Compensation: On-target earnings for this role range between $135,000 and $150,000 per year, depending on experience, which includes base salary and variable incentive compensation based on performance. At OpenSesame, we offer a comprehensive benefits package to employees upon hire, including ISOs, health insurance, 401(k) matching, and paid time off. We carefully consider a wide range of compensation factors, relying on market data to determine compensation and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience.

Benefits: Benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible PTO, 401(k) matching, incentive stock options, volunteer time off, Employee Resource Groups, and a generous professional development program with dedicated annual time off for learning and growth.

Equal Employment Opportunity: OpenSesame is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer that values and welcomes diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of various legally protected characteristics, including criminal history, and strive to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. We prioritize safety and security and may use your information accordingly, and you can contact us for assistance or accommodations during the job application process.

Pay Transparency: At OpenSesame, we prioritize pay transparency, fairness, and equity to create a positive and inclusive work environment, regularly reviewing our compensation practices to align with our values and goals. We provide competitive and fair compensation to our employees based on their skills, experience, and performance.

CPRA (California Candidates): When you submit your application, OpenSesame may collect and use your personal information in accordance with our privacy policy and the CPRA. This may include personal details and employment history, and will only be used for employment-related purposes. We may share this information with third-party service providers, but we will not sell it to third parties. If you have any questions or concerns, please contact us, and for more information on your rights under the CPRA, refer to our privacy policy or the California Attorney General's website.

About the Company

TalentPluto is a Y Combinator-backed startup building the hiring stack for high-growth companies. We run two connected products: a talent network that places engineering, go-to-market, and operations people into fast-moving startups, and an AI recruiting tool that lets a hiring team run candidate search, tiered enrichment, rubric-based scoring, and outbound campaigns directly from their assistant. We work with dozens of venture-backed startups across AI, developer tools, fintech, and healthcare. The team is small and founder-led, and interns work on live problems rather than practice ones.

The Opportunity

This is a design engineering internship, which means the same person decides how something should work and then builds it. You will take ideas that arrive as a sentence or a rough sketch and turn them into interfaces people actually use, owning the visual and interaction decisions along the way rather than waiting for a spec.

We care about craft here in a way that is easy to claim and harder to do: spacing, hierarchy, typography, and the small interaction details that make a product feel considered. Because the team is small and the surface is still being shaped, your judgment about how something should feel carries real weight, and you will see the result in front of users quickly.

Responsibilities

  • Design and build product surfaces end to end, from low-fidelity idea to shipped interface.
  • Own layout, typography, hierarchy, and interaction detail across the surfaces you build.
  • Implement in React, Next.js, and TypeScript, working with the backend services behind each surface.
  • Build and extend shared components so the product stays visually consistent as it grows.
  • Make interfaces work well across screen sizes and states, including the empty and error ones.

Requirements

  • Strong taste for product design, interaction design, and visual detail.
  • Experience building with React, Next.js, TypeScript, or similar frontend tools.
  • Comfort working from low-fidelity ideas and turning them into usable interfaces.
  • Strong understanding of layout, typography, hierarchy, and responsive design.
  • Has shipped design or frontend projects, whether independently, in class, or through prior work.
  • Clear communicator who can work independently in a remote environment.

Organization Overview:

Founded in 1981, the Committee to Protect Journalists (“CPJ”) is an independent, non-profit organization defending journalists worldwide without regard to their political ideology. Through its work to safeguard journalists, CPJ protects the rights of all people to have access to diverse and independent sources of information. For over four decades, CPJ has helped win the early release of imprisoned journalists, secure convictions in journalist murders, and enable legal reform in countries where free expression has deteriorated. CPJ’s widely cited database and reports have raised global awareness of attacks on press freedom. Learn more about CPJ’s fight to defend freedom of the press here

At CPJ, we are dedicated to upholding values of equity and free expression in both our internal operations and external endeavors. As a global organization headquartered in the United States, we aspire to build a diverse workplace and foster an inclusive and welcoming environment. We strive for our people to be representative of the global community on which we report and to equip them with the opportunities and resources they need to learn and succeed.

Job Summary:

The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) is hiring a Researcher - Western and Northern Europe (WNE) to join our Europe and Central Asia program. The position reports to the Program Coordinator, ECA, and is responsible for monitoring, researching, documenting, and responding to attacks on the press and other issues impacting press freedom in the region. The Researcher also supports the development of regional and sub-regional strategy, initiates and produces expert analysis on the region, represents CPJ publicly when required, and supports the program’s journalism assistance efforts.

This role requires a strong background in media, press freedom, and human rights in the ECA region, excellent research and writing skills, a solid understanding of journalistic standards, and the ability to work independently and proactively across the region. The Researcher collaborates with team members and other departments, following CPJ’s established guidelines and frameworks.

This position is based in the Europe/Central Asia region and will be hired via an Employer of Record.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Monitor, document and respond to press freedom abuses throughout the ECA region, with a focus on Western and Northern Europe.
  • Maintain and build relationships with journalists, human rights organisations, policymakers and other regional stakeholders.
  • Propose, direct and conduct research on press freedom issues in the ECA region.
  • Develop and execute advocacy strategies to advance press freedom in ECA, in coordination with Program Coordinator and Regional Director.
  • Initiate and write reports, advocacy documents, engaging social media content and other materials on press freedom issues in the region.
  • Review and assess requests for assistance from journalists in the region, in coordination with the Emergencies team.
  • Represent CPJ at conferences and meetings with authorities, journalists, partners, policymakers and other stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with CPJ’s global teams, including Advocacy, Research, and Assistance, to ensure coordinated organizational impact.
  • Provide translation of interviews, documents, and other materials between English and relevant local languages, as needed.
  • Perform other duties within the scope of CPJ’s research and advocacy mandate as requested by the Program Coordinator or Regional Director.

Qualifications & Competencies:

Required:

  • Minimum of five years experience in researching, reporting, and publishing on global human rights and politics, or equivalent experience in advocacy and humanitarian assistance.
  • Strong understanding of Europe and Central Asia issues, including media and human rights.
  • Excellent English writing and reporting skills.
  • Proficiency in at least one other language relevant to the position.
  • Excellent interpersonal, organisational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to act with integrity, professionalism, and confidentiality.
  • Significant experience working with governments and other policymakers.

  • We communicate with clarity and credibility, serving as trusted advisors to GTM teams and leadership.
  • We believe the best results come from tight collaboration and shared learning, supporting one another through peer problem-solving, documentation, and knowledge-sharing so the entire organization gets better together.

About the Sales Operations Manager, Channel & Partnerships role:

The Sales Operations Manager, Channel & Partnerships is the operational partner responsible for helping OpenSesame scale its partner business with greater clarity, efficiency, accountability, and predictability.

This role partners closely with Strategic Partner Managers, Partner Development, the Partner Program Manager, Revenue Operations, Sales, Finance, Business Systems, Legal, Enablement, Marketing, and Product to improve how partner-sourced, partner-influenced, reseller, OEM, referral, and co-sell motions operate from partner lead submission through quote-to-cash.

This is a manager-level individual contributor role with no direct reports. The role requires manager-level judgment, strong business partnership, analytical depth, and the ability to influence change through process, data, systems, automation, and AI-enabled workflows. This is not a reporting-only role or a tactical support desk. The right person will diagnose partner process friction, improve tool adoption, clarify ownership, strengthen partner attribution, and turn messy data into actionable insights that help the partner business grow.

Success in this role means partner leaders trust the data, Partner Sales Managers have clear operating views, partners submit leads through the right platform, quote-to-cash processes are understood, and leadership can clearly see what is working, what is at risk, and where to focus next.

Performance Objectives

Within 30 Days: Understand, Diagnose, and Prioritize

  • Build a deep understanding of OpenSesame’s partner ecosystem, including reseller, OEM, referral, partner-sourced, partner-influenced, and co-sell motions.
  • Establish strong relationships with Partner Sales Managers, Partner Development, the Partner Program Manager, Sales, Finance, Business Systems, Legal, Enablement, Marketing, Product, and RevOps.
  • Audit current partner lead submission, routing, attribution, opportunity management, handoff, reporting, and quote-to-cash processes.
  • Assess adoption and utilization of key partner tools and workflows, including Euler, Crossbeam, Salesforce, Gong, Looker, ZoomInfo, Clay, and related GTM systems.
  • Identify friction points impacting partner lead submission, partner visibility, SPM productivity, reporting accuracy, quote-to-cash execution, and forecast confidence.
  • Deliver a current-state assessment with prioritized recommendations, including quick wins and longer-term operating improvements.

Within 60 Days: Improve Process, Visibility, and Adoption

  • Refine partner lead and opportunity workflows to improve routing accuracy, attribution, pipeline visibility, and accountability.
  • Establish clearer standards for partner lead submission through Euler, including required fields, SLAs, review process, ownership, and follow-up expectations.
  • Improve use of Crossbeam to support account mapping, overlap analysis, co-sell opportunity identification, partner prioritization, and joint pipeline visibility.
  • Build or improve reporting views for Partner Sales Managers, Partner Development, Partner Program leadership, Sales leadership, Finance, and RevOps.
  • Partner with Business Systems to scope CRM, Euler, Crossbeam, and workflow improvements that reduce manual work and improve data quality.
  • Identify automation or AI-enabled opportunities to streamline partner operations, improve lead hygiene, summarize partner performance, or surface pipeline risk faster.
  • Align with Enablement and the Partner Program Manager on internal and partner-facing communication, training, and adoption reinforcement.

Beyond 90 Days: Scale Partner Operations and Strategic Impact

  • Own ongoing operational health across partner lead submission, attribution, opportunity management, reporting, and quote-to-cash workflows.
  • Build durable reporting that helps leadership understand partner pipeline quality, conversion, revenue contribution, account overlap, and growth opportunities.
  • Surface insights on partner performance, partner fit, source quality, deal velocity, conversion, attribution, and partner profitability.
  • Support Partner Development with data-backed insights to identify, prioritize, and evaluate potential new partners.
  • Support Partner Sales Managers with clear views into partner account activity, pipeline, performance, whitespace, and expansion opportunities.
  • Partner with Finance, Legal, Deal Desk, and Sales to improve operational clarity across OEM and reseller quote-to-cash processes.
  • Drive measurable improvements in tool adoption, workflow efficiency, partner lead compliance, reporting accuracy, and partner pipeline visibility.
  • Be viewed by Partner leadership as a trusted operating partner who brings clarity, urgency, and practical solutions.

Ongoing Responsibilities

Partner Pipeline, Attribution & Rules of Engagement

  • Own operational visibility into partner-sourced, partner-influenced, reseller, OEM, referral, and co-sell pipeline.
  • Improve partner lead submission, routing, tracking, and attribution across Euler, Crossbeam, Salesforce, and related systems.
  • Support and operationalize partner attribution rules, including source, influence, referral, reseller, OEM, and co-sell motions.
  • Help maintain partner rules of engagement, including lead submission requirements, ownership, AE/SPM handoff expectations, response SLAs, conflict resolution, and exception handling.
  • Identify attribution gaps, duplicate submissions, unclear ownership, inconsistent crediting, stale opportunities, or missing partner data.

Partner Tool Adoption, Automation & AI

  • Drive adoption of partner tools and workflows by making processes clear, useful, and easy to follow for internal teams and external partners.
  • Diagnose friction across Euler, Crossbeam, Salesforce, reporting, handoffs, and quote-to-cash workflows.
  • Partner with Business Systems, Analytics, and Enablement to scope, test, and roll out system or workflow improvements.
  • Identify opportunities to use automation and AI-enabled workflows to reduce manual work, improve data quality, and surface insights faster.
  • Explore use cases such as partner performance summaries, lead quality checks, account overlap insights, partner QBR prep, pipeline risk alerts, quote-to-cash prompts, and executive reporting.

Reporting, Analytics & Strategic Insights

  • Build and maintain reporting that helps Partner leadership understand what is working, what is at risk, and where to focus.
  • Analyze partner pipeline, conversion, sales cycle, win rates, deal velocity, source quality, attribution, account overlap, and revenue contribution.
  • Support partner QBRs, business reviews, annual planning, and performance discussions with clear, data-backed insights.
  • Translate messy or incomplete data into executive-ready recommendations: what changed, why it changed, what is at risk, and what action is recommended.

Partner Program, Planning & Growth Support

  • Support the Partner Program Manager with operational infrastructure for partner tiers, program rules, incentives, enablement, compliance, and performance measurement.
  • Support Partner Development with analysis to identify and prioritize prospective partners based on fit, account overlap, market opportunity, and revenue potential.
  • Support Partner Sales Managers in managing and expanding partner relationships through account visibility, pipeline insights, partner activity reporting, and process clarity.
  • Build visibility across the partner lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, enablement, activation, pipeline creation, revenue contribution, and expansion.

Quote-to-Cash & Cross-Functional Operations

  • Build operational understanding of quote-to-cash requirements across OEM, reseller, referral, and other partner motions.
  • Partner with Finance, Legal, Deal Desk, Business Systems, and Sales to clarify requirements, reduce friction, and improve handoffs.
  • Improve visibility into partner deal economics, including discounts, reseller margins, referral fees, OEM terms, payment obligations, and revenue recognition considerations where applicable.
  • Translate business needs into clear requirements for process, reporting, systems, and enablement improvements.

You might notice we don’t have the typical list of requirements and buzzwords here. That’s intentional.

We’re looking for proven examples from your career that show you can do this job, that you’ve built systems, driven alignment, and created impact at scale. When you look back a year from now, you’ll know you’ve made OpenSesame better, faster, and stronger because of your leadership.

Although it should go without saying (but it doesn’t), OpenSesame is an equal opportunity employer and we strive to create a welcoming, inclusive environment that celebrates diversity.

We use AI. For real. Every team at OpenSesame works with AI tools daily, not as a buzzword, but as practice. You'll build fluency that most companies are still talking about adopting, with hands-on training and clear guardrails to experiment responsibly. AI amplifies your creativity and judgment. It doesn't replace them. The skills you build here travel with you.

Location: This position can be based anywhere in the US. We operate as a remote-first company, and invest in mandatory all-company meetings several times a year in addition to required team travel as necessary.

Performance Driven: We're looking for self-starters with a track record of delivering excellent results, but we're highly selective about who we hire. We don't focus on typical job requirements, instead, we're interested in specific examples from your past experiences. All positions can be based anywhere in the US, and require up to 15 days of travel per year, with senior management and leadership teams requiring up to 35 days.

Compensation: On-target earnings for this role range between $135,000 and $150,000 per year, depending on experience, which includes base salary and variable incentive compensation based on performance. At OpenSesame, we offer a comprehensive benefits package to employees upon hire, including ISOs, health insurance, 401(k) matching, and paid time off. We carefully consider a wide range of compensation factors, relying on market data to determine compensation and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience.

Benefits: Benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible PTO, 401(k) matching, incentive stock options, volunteer time off, Employee Resource Groups, and a generous professional development program with dedicated annual time off for learning and growth.

Equal Employment Opportunity: OpenSesame is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer that values and welcomes diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of various legally protected characteristics, including criminal history, and strive to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. We prioritize safety and security and may use your information accordingly, and you can contact us for assistance or accommodations during the job application process.

Pay Transparency: At OpenSesame, we prioritize pay transparency, fairness, and equity to create a positive and inclusive work environment, regularly reviewing our compensation practices to align with our values and goals. We provide competitive and fair compensation to our employees based on their skills, experience, and performance.

CPRA (California Candidates): When you submit your application, OpenSesame may collect and use your personal information in accordance with our privacy policy and the CPRA. This may include personal details and employment history, and will only be used for employment-related purposes.
